blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton

steps.body: Tank, bowl, seal, flange and line.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.body: In many 1950s Skokie homes, the toilet sits on a cast iron flange connected to the original drain. Over time, the flange corrodes and the bolts lose their grip, so the toilet rocks and the seal fails. We repair or replace the flange before setting the toilet. It's the difference between a toilet that stays tight and one that leaks again in a year.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Toilet Work
blocks.body: Small repairs are quick. Replacing a corroded flange takes longer. A new toilet depends on the model. We check and quote a flat price.

items.preview: Loose bolts or a damaged flange.
items.answer: Usually loose bolts or a corroded flange. Rocking breaks the wax seal, so it's worth fixing early.

items.q: Why does my toilet clog so often?
items.preview: An older toilet or a line problem.
items.answer: Older low-flow toilets clog more. If other drains are slow too, the main line is the problem.

items.q: Should I replace or repair my toilet?
items.preview: If it's cracked or keeps failing, replace it.
items.answer: If the bowl or tank is cracked or it keeps needing repairs, replacing it is usually better.

items.q: Can you install a comfort-height toilet?
items.answer: Yes. We install comfort-height and other models with a new seal and supply line.

items.q: Can you install a toilet with a smaller footprint?
items.answer: Yes. Compact models work well in small bathrooms.

items.q: Can you replace a wax ring?
items.answer: Yes. We pull the toilet, replace the seal and reset it tight.

items.q: How much does toilet repair cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on the problem. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what's wrong and whether you're repairing or replacing. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
